title: Control-flow flattening
description: Flattening destroys the program's natural control flow: all basic blocks become cases in one big switch inside a dispatcher loop, with the 'next block' tracked in a state variable. The CFG becomes a star — static analysis sees soup, while the program runs identically.
method: Split into basic blocks; wrap in while(switch(state)); each block sets the next state; the dispatcher obscures the real flow.
usage: Apply to sensitive functions; combine with opaque predicates; measure the performance cost.

demo.code:
print('original: if/else chain (readable CFG)')
print('flattened: while True: switch(state) {case 0: ...; state=3; ...}')
print('same semantics, CFG unrecognizable')

title: String and constant encryption
description: Plaintext strings ('license expired', API keys, URLs) are reverser gold. Encrypting all constants — decrypted at runtime just before use, wiped after — removes the easy landmarks. The binary's strings section becomes noise.
method: Encrypt constants at build; emit decrypt-on-use stubs; wipe after use; rotate keys per build.
usage: Encrypt all sensitive constants; JIT-decrypt to minimize exposure window.

demo.code:
print('strings section: no "license", no URLs (all encrypted)')
print('runtime: decrypt -> use -> wipe (exposure: microseconds)')

title: Mixed boolean-arithmetic (MBA) expressions
description: MBA replaces simple operations with convoluted equivalents: x + y becomes a mess of XORs, ANDs, and multiplications that's provably equal but painful to simplify. Reversers' deobfuscators choke on MBA; it's the arithmetic equivalent of control-flow flattening.
method: Rewrite arithmetic as MBA identities; verify equivalence; apply to license checks and crypto-adjacent code.
usage: Apply to critical computations; verify the MBA identity's correctness formally.

demo.code:
print('x + y  ->  (x ^ y) + 2*(x & y)  ->  MBA-expanded 14-term form')
print('provably equal; simplifiers struggle')

title: Code packing and encryption
description: Packers compress/encrypt the executable and prepend a stub that unpacks it at runtime — the on-disk binary reveals nothing. UPX is the benign famous one; malicious packers add anti-analysis. For protection, packing is the outer layer: what's on disk isn't what's running.
method: Compress/encrypt the binary; stub unpacks to memory at load; execute from memory; wipe the stub's keys.
usage: Use as the outer layer; custom packers beat known ones (analysts have UPX unpackers).

demo.code:
print('on disk: 2MB encrypted blob + 50KB stub')
print('at runtime: unpacked to memory, executed, keys wiped')

title: Watermarking and fingerprinting
description: Obfuscation hides; watermarking traces: embed per-customer fingerprints in the binary (instruction choices, basic-block orderings) so leaked copies identify the leaker. The code runs identically for everyone but each build is uniquely traceable.
method: Vary codegen choices per customer (register allocation, block order); record the fingerprint; extract from suspect binaries.
usage: Fingerprint high-value distributions; keep the fingerprint database secure.

demo.code:
print('build for customer C7: block order [3,1,2], regalloc seed 77')
print('leaked binary analyzed -> fingerprint matches C7')

title: Obfuscation measurement (potency/resilience)
description: Collberg's framework measures obfuscation: potency (how much harder to understand), resilience (how hard to deobfuscate automatically), cost (performance hit). Measuring turns obfuscation from vibes into engineering — you know what each layer buys and what it costs.
method: Measure before/after complexity metrics; test against deobfuscators; track the cost budget; drop layers that don't pay.
usage: Measure every layer; keep what pays; the cost budget is real.

demo.code:
print('flattening: potency +62%, resilience high, cost +8% -> KEEP')
print('MBA: potency +40%, cost +31% -> DROP (over budget)')

title: Anti-debugging techniques
description: Obfuscated code fights back against debuggers: timing checks (rdtsc deltas reveal single-stepping), debugger-presence APIs (IsDebuggerPresent, ptrace), and exception-based control flow that breaks under debuggers. Each technique is bypassable, but layered they raise the cost of dynamic analysis.
method: Layer timing checks, presence detection, and anti-attach; respond by degrading (not crashing — crashes confirm the check worked).
usage: Layer several; respond subtly; assume each will be bypassed eventually.

demo.code:
import time
t0 = time.perf_counter()
# ... protected region ...
dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'region took {dt*1e6:.0f}us', '-> debugger suspected' if dt > 0.1 else '-> clean')

title: Symbol stripping and renaming
description: The first obfuscation everyone applies: strip symbols, rename everything to meaningless identifiers. It doesn't stop a determined reverser, but it removes the free documentation — function names like 'verify_license' become 'a1b2c3', and the reverser starts blind.
method: Strip debug symbols; rename identifiers systematically; remove metadata; verify the build still links.
usage: Always strip release builds; renaming is table stakes, not protection.

demo.code:
print('before: verify_license(), check_expiry()')
print('after: a1(), b7() (stripped, renamed)')
